brief: Goldman Sachs argues AI capex and rising government borrowing are competing for capital, pushing up its cost: 30-year German and Japanese yields were near zero in 2022 and equity risk premia have fallen to late-1990s levels, though US and Japanese ERP has bounced off recent lows. It is the speed of yield moves, not their level, that hits stocks; a 2-standard-deviation move (about 50bps a month) explains the recent pullback. Earnings growth has offset this so far: S&P forward P/E fell from 22x to 19x even as the market sits near highs. Hyperscaler capex has eaten into free cash flow, pushing AA-rated issuers and AI borrowers into debt and convertible markets, and GS raised its US IG issuance forecast to $2.3tn. Mega-cap tech has de-rated toward the market average, but GS argues this is not a 2008-style bubble because profits, balance sheets and compute demand (Microsoft, Nvidia) remain strong; the risk is an earnings slowdown, not valuation. GS stays neutral on equities over 3 months, overweight over 12, and favors diversification as regional and stock correlations broaden.
